_comment: THE canonical version-matrix construct catalogue (VERSION_TEST_MATRIX_DESIGN.md §10 #5). Each entry: a minimal program exercising ONE construct + its edition metadata. VersionMatrixTests computes the expected outcome per (construct × edition): compiles iff introducedIn <= V and (removedIn null or V < removedIn). The human-readable VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md and the in-code ConstructDialectStatus registry are renderings of THIS file — extend it here, never fork. 'vcr' cites the VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row/section or the introducing standard where the doc has no row (it covers 2002→2023 deltas only). OPTIONAL 'status': 'pending' = catalogued (edition metadata frozen by the drift tests) but not yet implemented — the matrix SKIPS its compile assertions until the owning roadmap phase lands and flips it active (the one pending mechanism, shared with the corpus discovery manifests). Vendor-dialect constructs live in vendor-constructs.json (owner decision 2), never here.

constructs.description: Nucleus MOVE/DISPLAY — edition-invariant since COBOL-85
constructs.citation: edition-invariant baseline
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. NUC.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 W PIC X(5) VALUE "HI".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    MOVE "BYE" TO W.
    DISPLAY W.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.citation: ISO §14.9.30 Format 1; VCR rows 29/108 gate after-OPEN behavior

PROGRAM-ID. RP.

constructs.description: EXIT SECTION (ISO §14.9.14 Format 4 / §14.9.14.4 GR7) — a COBOL-2002 structured-procedure exit transferring control to the end of the current section (firing its PERFORM/SORT/USE return mechanism); introduced 2002.
constructs.citation: ISO §14.9.14.2 Format 4 / §14.9.14.4 GR7 — COBOL-2002 structured-exit introduction (VCR has no 85→2002 rows; derived from the 2002 standard)

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
DRIVER SECTION.
D1.
    PERFORM WORK-SEC.
    STOP RUN.
WORK-SEC SECTION.
W1.
    EXIT SECTION.
W2.
    DISPLAY "W2".

constructs.description: EXIT PARAGRAPH (ISO §14.9.14.2 Format 4 / §14.9.14.4 GR6) — a COBOL-2002 structured-procedure exit transferring control to the implicit CONTINUE at the end of the current paragraph; introduced 2002 (the 85 EXIT is only Format 1, §14.9.14.3 SR1).
constructs.citation: ISO §14.9.14.2 Format 4 / §14.9.14.4 GR6 — COBOL-2002 structured-exit introduction (VCR has no 85→2002 rows; derived from the 2002 standard)

P2.

constructs.description: EXIT PERFORM [CYCLE] (ISO §14.9.14.2 Format 3 / §14.9.14.4 GR5a) — a COBOL-2002 structured-procedure exit leaving (or cycling) the most closely preceding inline PERFORM; introduced 2002 (the 85 EXIT is only Format 1, §14.9.14.3 SR1). CYCLE is confined to an inline PERFORM by §14.9.14.3 SR8 and rides the same gate.
constructs.citation: ISO §14.9.14.2 Format 3 / §14.9.14.4 GR5a — COBOL-2002 structured-exit introduction (VCR has no 85→2002 rows; derived from the 2002 standard)
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMEXPERF.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9 VALUE 0.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    PERFORM UNTIL N > 5
        ADD 1 TO N
        IF N = 3 EXIT PERFORM END-IF
    END-PERFORM.
    DISPLAY N.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.description: ALLOCATE statement (dynamic storage), ISO §14.9.3 - introduced 2002. ACTIVE: both formats bind (n CHARACTERS RETURNING p -> a fresh StorageCell window pointer, GR1 round-up / GR2 <=0 -> NULL no EC / GR6 INITIALIZED zero-fill; based-item -> the implicit pointer takes a cell of the template width, GR3/GR4a/GR4b) and the based INITIALIZED form lowers per GR7 to the spec's INITIALIZE ... WITH FILLER ALL TO VALUE THEN TO DEFAULT expansion (a BoundSequence over the ONE INITIALIZE mechanism; golden 2002/allocate_initialized). INITIALIZED is a phrase of this gated statement - no separate matrix row (the phrase-level precedent).
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. AL.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
77 P USAGE POINTER.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    ALLOCATE 100 CHARACTERS RETURNING P.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.description: FREE statement (release ALLOCATEd storage), ISO §14.9.15 - introduced 2002. ACTIVE as of Phase-4b increment 2 (DEVLOG 617): per-operand GR1 three-way (release-and-null / NULL no-op / nonfatal EC-STORAGE-NOT-ALLOC through the TurnState-gated status block); SR1 data-pointer operands only (the vendor FREE based-item form rejects 0869); a freed cell's dangling aliases fail loud at the next dereference (EC-BOUND-PTR).

constructs.description: INVOKE (OO method call), ISO §14.9.23 — introduced 2002. LIVE since the Phase-3 spine part 2 (DEVLOG 601): Class NEW RETURNING → new C(); no-arg instance INVOKE → virtual call behind the EC-OO-NULL guard (§14.9.23.4 GR5); USING/RETURNING marshaling (slice 2), SELF/SUPER (3b), factory and universal dispatch stage loud. Below 2002 the grammar gate + W1.5 mapping name the edition (0900).

constructs.description: GOBACK … WITH {ERROR|NORMAL} STATUS [id|lit] phrase, ISO §14.9.18.2 — a COBOL-2023 addition (annex item 32: GOBACK now allows the same status phrase as the STOP statement; §14.9.18.4 GR3 routes a main-program GOBACK to STOP semantics). Distinct edition from the 2002 STOP-status phrase — the shared statusPhrase rule is 2002-gated on STOP, 2023 on GOBACK. GOBACK is valid at 2014 so the below-2023 witness isolates the status phrase.

constructs.description: USAGE PACKED-DECIMAL WITH NO SIGN (ISO §13.18.60.4 GR11) — a COBOL-2023 addition: the packed item reserves no trailing sign nibble (storage = ceil(Digits/2) bytes), the value is always zero-or-positive, and SR31 forbids an 'S' picture. NO SIGN is a modifier on Usage.Packed (which exists at every edition) so the gate is recognition-based on the parsed noSignPhrase, not a resolved-usage key.
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. NOSGN.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 W PIC 9(6) PACKED-DECIMAL WITH NO SIGN.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    MOVE 12 TO W.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.description: SET [SIZE OF] data-name TO n (ISO §14.9.39 Format 16) — a COBOL-2023 addition: set the current length of a DYNAMIC LENGTH elementary item (growing space-fills the added positions, GR39; shrinking drops trailing positions). Semantic gate on the BoundSetSize node (the target must be dynamic-length), covering both the explicit SIZE OF form and the bare re-routed form. The DYNAMIC LENGTH clause itself is 2014, but the SET-length form is 2023.
constructs.citation: ISO §14.9.39 Format 16 (GR37-39); Annex E.3.3 item — the dynamic-length SET
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. SETSZ.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 D PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    MOVE "HI" TO D.
    SET SIZE OF D TO 4.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.description: COBOL word length ceiling raised to 63 characters (ISO §8.3.2.1) — a COBOL-2023 RELAXATION (E.3.3 item 11: was 31 in 2002/2014, 30 in 1985). A 42-character user-defined word compiles at 2023 and is rejected below 2023 (COBOLNET1567 — a ceiling that TIGHTENS below 2023, the opposite direction from a new-feature introduction gate). A word longer than 63 characters is rejected at EVERY edition.
constructs.citation: ISO §8.3.2.1; Annex E.3.3 item 11 (the 63-character relaxation)
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. WL63.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 THIS-IS-A-FORTY-CHARACTER-LONG-DATANAME-XX PIC 9 VALUE 0.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.description: CONTINUE AFTER arithmetic-expression SECONDS (ISO §14.9.9) — a COBOL-2023 addition: a timed pause. Plain CONTINUE is 1985-continuous; only the AFTER … SECONDS phrase is gated. A negative interval is forced to 0 (GR1a) and sets the nonfatal EC-CONTINUE-LESS-THAN-ZERO under CHECKING ON (GR1b).
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. CONTA.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.description: PERFORM … UNTIL EXIT (ISO §14.9.28.4 GR11) — a COBOL-2023 addition: an unconditional infinite loop (a condition that never becomes true). Plain UNTIL condition is edition-invariant; only the EXIT alternative is gated. Escape is by EXIT PERFORM (inline) or GOBACK/STOP RUN (out-of-line).
constructs.citation: ISO §14.9.28.2 until-phrase / §14.9.28.4 GR11; Annex E.3.3 item 37
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. PUE.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 N PIC 9 VALUE 0.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    PERFORM UNTIL EXIT
        ADD 1 TO N
        IF N = 2 EXIT PERFORM END-IF
    END-PERFORM.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.description: The >>LEAP-SECOND [ON|OFF] compiler directive (ISO §7.3.17) — a COBOL-2002 compiler-directive introduction (§7.3): with ON in effect a formatted-time argument's seconds subfield may be 60 (§15.3.3.3) and a standard numeric time form value is bounded at 86,401 (§7.3.17.4 GR4) instead of 86,400 (GR5); the reported side (a 60 in the seconds position of the clock functions, SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT >= 86,400) is implementor-defined and answered never (A.1 item 112). A text-manipulation-stage directive consumed by LeapSecondDirectiveProcessor; the introduction gate rejects the directive below 2002 (kb/Work PB65).
constructs.source:
>>LEAP-SECOND ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. LEAPS.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 R PIC 9(6).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           MOVE 86400 TO R.
           DISPLAY R.
           STOP RUN.

constructs.description: The >>REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH {ON|OFF} compiler directive (ISO §7.3.23) — a COBOL-2023 addition (Annex E.3.3 item 23): when ON, a reference modification MAY have a zero-length result (§8.4.3.3.4 item 5c); when OFF/omitted (the default) a zero-length ref-mod raises EC-BOUND-REF-MOD (§7.3.23.3 GR1). A text-manipulation-stage directive consumed by RefModZeroLengthDirectiveProcessor and folded per source line; the introduction gate rejects the directive below 2023.
constructs.citation: ISO §7.3.23; §8.4.3.3.4 item 5c; Annex E.3.3 item 23
constructs.source:
>>REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RMZL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 W PIC X(5) VALUE "HELLO".
       01 R PIC X(5).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           MOVE W (3:0) TO R.
           DISPLAY R.
           STOP RUN.

constructs.description: The >>FLAG-14 { ALL | option... } { ON | OFF } migration-flagging directive (ISO §7.3.15) — a COBOL-2023 addition: Annex E.2 item 5 lists FLAG-14 among the compiler-directive words new to 2023. It directs the implementor's warning mechanism to flag 2014-to-2023 incompatibilities (GR1). Recognized and collected by FlagDirectiveProcessor and folded per option per source line by FlagState (FlagConformancePass emits the per-option COBOLNET1621 warning); the introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2023.
constructs.citation: ISO §7.3.15; Annex E.2 item 5 (compiler-directive words added in 2023)
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. FLG14.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
       >>FLAG-14 READ-PREVIOUS ON
           DISPLAY "Y".
           STOP RUN.

constructs.description: The >>FLAG-02 { ALL | option... } { ON | OFF } migration-flagging directive (ISO §7.3.14) — introduced in COBOL-2014 to flag 2002-to-2014 incompatibilities (GR1; the directive references the 2014 edition, and Annex E.2 item 5 lists only FLAG-14 as new to 2023, so FLAG-02 predates 2023). It is OBSOLETE (NOT removed) in COBOL-2023 — §7.3.14.1 NOTE: 'an obsolete element in this Working Draft International Standard and is to be deleted from the next edition'. Per §4.2.13 an implementation SHALL SUPPORT obsolete elements, so at 2023 it STILL COMPILES and carries the COBOLNET0903 obsolete warning (never a 0902 removal error). Modeled introducedIn=2014 + obsoleteIn=2023: the introduction gate rejects below 2014, the obsolete gate warns at 2023.
constructs.citation: ISO §7.3.14; §7.3.14.1 NOTE (obsolete in 2023); §4.2.13 (obsolete elements shall be supported + warned)
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. FLG02.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
       >>FLAG-02 I-O-STATUS-07 ON
           DISPLAY "Y".
           STOP RUN.

constructs.description: The >>COBOL-WORDS { EQUATE l1 WITH l2 | UNDEFINE l3 | SUBSTITUTE l4 BY l5 | RESERVE l6 } compiler directive (ISO §7.3.10; Annex D.12; Annex E.3.3 item 12) — a COBOL-2023 addition (Annex E.2 item 5 lists COBOL-WORDS among the compiler-directive words new to 2023). It modifies which words are reserved / context-sensitive / intrinsic-function words and prohibits specified user-defined words, per compilation group, during the text-manipulation stage. Recognized and parsed by CobolWordsDirectiveProcessor into a CobolWordsMap consumed by the post-lex token rewriter + the composed ReservedWordSet + intrinsic-name resolution; the introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2023.
constructs.citation: ISO §7.3.10; Annex D.12; Annex E.3.3 item 12; Annex E.2 item 5 (compiler-directive words added in 2023)
constructs.source:
>>COBOL-WORDS RESERVE "FOO"
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. CWORDS.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.

constructs.description: A strongly-typed EXTERNAL type declaration (ISO §13.18.22.3 SR1/SR5; §8.5.3; Annex E.3 item 10) — a COBOL-2023 addition. E.3 item 10 states external items 'could not be strongly typed' before 2023, so it is specifically the STRONG+EXTERNAL combination on a level-1 TYPEDEF that is new; SR5 forces a strongly-typed external record's type to itself be a strong external type declaration. A WEAK 'TYPEDEF IS EXTERNAL' (no STRONG) was already valid in COBOL-2002 (§13.18.58.3 SR3) and is NOT gated. Gated on the co-occurrence of the EXTERNAL clause with a STRONG TYPEDEF clause on one level-1 data description entry. Below 2023 the strong external type declaration is rejected.
constructs.vcr: VCR row 63 (strongly-typed EXTERNAL type declaration — 2023 introduction; weak external TYPEDEF stays COBOL-2002)
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. XTD.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 T IS EXTERNAL TYPEDEF STRONG.
          05 A PIC X(4).
       01 R TYPE T IS EXTERNAL.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           STOP RUN.

constructs.description: A non-zero numeric literal in the VALUE clause of a numeric-edited item (ISO §13.18.63 SR6) — a COBOL-2023 capability (Annex E.3.3 item 43): the literal is converted to its numeric-edited form per the MOVE rules. Below 2023 a numeric-edited VALUE required an alphanumeric edited-image literal. SR6 exempts the figurative constant ZERO and the integer/decimal forms of the literal zero at ALL editions, so only a NON-ZERO numeric literal is gated.
constructs.display: numeric-literal VALUE for a numeric-edited item
constructs.citation: ISO §13.18.63 SR6; Annex E.3.3 item 43

constructs.description: An alphanumeric edited-image literal in the VALUE clause of a numeric-edited item that EXCEEDS the PICTURE's edited size (ISO §13.18.63 SR4/SR5) — before COBOL-2023 it was stored truncated (the 'unclear value'), at 2023 it is checked and rejected (Annex E.2 item 27). Modeled as removedIn=2023 (compiles at 85/2002/2014 truncated, rejects at 2023 with COBOLNET1570; --permissive downgrades to a warning). The national/alphanumeric class mismatch is the separate COBOLNET0898 check.

constructs.description: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE(file-connector-name) with an optional file-connector-name argument (ISO §15.28.2/.3/.4 r2) — a COBOL-2023 addition (Annex E.3.3 item 25): it returns the NAMED FD connector's I-O status + SELECT-spelled name, or two spaces if that connector was never opened/attempted/accessed. The no-argument base form is 2002. The argument form is gated below 2023.

constructs.description: A MERGE statement in the output procedure of another MERGE, or the input/output procedure of a file-format SORT, is PROHIBITED as of COBOL-2023 (ISO §14.9.24; Annex E.2 item 20 — the prior standard allowed it with conflicting rules, and SORT already disallowed it). A bind-time procedure-range cross-pass (VersionConformancePass.GateMergeInSortMergeProc) rejects it at >=2023 with COBOLNET1572; below 2023 the runtime EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE seam is the (checking-off) dynamic net. Modeled as a removedIn=2023 construct (compiles at 85/2002/2014, rejects at 2023).
constructs.display: MERGE in a SORT/MERGE input or output procedure
constructs.citation: ISO §14.9.24; Annex E.2 item 20
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. MERGEPRO.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT F1 ASSIGN TO "mp1.txt".
           SELECT F2 ASSIGN TO "mp2.txt".
           SELECT F3 ASSIGN TO "mp3.txt".
           SELECT F4 ASSIGN TO "mp4.txt".
           SELECT FO ASSIGN TO "mpo.txt".
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       SD S1.
       01 SR1 PIC X(5).
       SD S2.
       01 SR2 PIC X(5).
       FD F1.
       01 R1 PIC X(5).
       FD F2.
       01 R2 PIC X(5).
       FD F3.
       01 R3 PIC X(5).
       FD F4.
       01 R4 PIC X(5).
       FD FO.
       01 RO PIC X(5).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           MERGE S1 ON ASCENDING KEY SR1
               USING F1 F2
               OUTPUT PROCEDURE OUT-PROC.
           STOP RUN.
       OUT-PROC.
           MERGE S2 ON ASCENDING KEY SR2
               USING F3 F4
               GIVING FO.

constructs.description: The boolean shift operators B-SHIFT-L / B-SHIFT-R / B-SHIFT-LC / B-SHIFT-RC (ISO §8.8.2 rule 8) — a COBOL-2023 addition (strictly later than the 2002 boolean operators B-AND/B-OR/B-XOR/B-NOT). Logical shift fills boolean 0; circular shift rotates. The second operand is an integer; the result length is the first operand's length (rule 9). Recognition-based gate (HasShiftOp) at the COMPUTE F2 / primaryCondition altitude, distinct from the boolean-operators-2002 gate.
constructs.citation: ISO §8.8.2 rule 8 / Table 4; Annex E.2 (reserved-word additions)
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. BSH.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 A PIC 1(4) VALUE B"1100".
01 R PIC 1(4).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
